events.title: Ageing Badly
events.description: ‘Ageing Badly’ challenges assumptions that the goal of one’s later years is to age well or ‘successfully’, a message that, since the 1960s, has become pervasive, naturalized in medicine, social theory, and popular culture. Ageing badly, by contrast, encompasses a range of uncomfortable and idiosyncratic ways in which art works, bodies, artists, and ideas, such as ‘the 1960s’, have aged over time. The language of ageing is deeply entangled with those concerning time, history, and the body—languages that have in turn shaped the field of art history and feminist interventions in the field.

events.title: Asserting Access to Government: Black Residents’ Demands for Government Protection from Interracial Violence in Richmond, Virginia, 1865–1867
events.description: This dissertation chapter examines interracial violence in Richmond, Virginia, during the early years of Reconstruction. Immediately after the Civil War, Richmond was policed by both federal soldiers and a newly professionalizing city police force. White civilians, Union soldiers, and members of the city police force frequently used violence against Black residents in order to discipline their behavior in public. Using Freedmen’s Bureau records, military records, and newspapers, this chapter discusses how Black Richmonders advocated for themselves in the wake of such interracial violence.
